title: Incident Bot v2: add “Recent deploys” context card (rollout phase + canary health + PR/commit links)
creator: Miles Thornton
description:
Add a “Recent deploys” card to Incident Bot v2 output in #incidents / #eng-oncall threads. Card should automatically attach deploy context for the affected service + region (and where applicable pool) to reduce MTTR on deploy regressions.

Motivation:
- Recent incident threads repeatedly lacked basic deploy context (what changed? was it canary? did rollout finish?) which slowed triage.
- We want “first 5 minutes” context standardized and fast, without responders having to jump between CI, GitHub, and rollout tooling.

Scope:
- Fetch recent deploy events for a service/region (last N=3 by default; configurable) and render a Slack card with:
  - service name + environment + region
  - current rollout phase (canary / staged / full / rollback in progress)
  - canary status (pass/fail/unknown) with a short reason when available
  - deployed version identifiers (image tag and/or commit SHA)
  - links: GitHub commit, GitHub PR (if resolvable), and internal deploy/rollout page in Console
- Ensure card rendering works in both initial incident context message and on-demand refresh action.

Non-goals:
- No deep analysis of performance changes in this ticket (just surface deploy metadata + links).
- No changes to how deploy metadata is produced (assumes backend source of truth is available).

Primary stakeholders:
- SRE: Rafael Mendes, Sean Gallagher
- Release Eng: Connor O'Brien
- Bot/Tooling: Dylan Brooks

Relevant artifacts:
- GitHub: incident-bot PR draft: sources/github/incident-bot/pr-1842-add-deploy-context-block.json
- Backend metadata export: sources/github/redwood/pr-29104-export-deploy-metadata-to-incident-bot.json
acceptance_criteria:
- Bot posts a “Recent deploys” card within the incident context payload for identified service+region.
- Card shows the last 3 deploys (newest first) with timestamp, rollout phase, and version identifiers.
- Canary status is summarized as one of: PASS | FAIL | IN_PROGRESS | UNKNOWN, with a short detail string if provided (e.g., “p95 latency +18% vs baseline”).
- Card includes working links:
  - GitHub commit link (if commit SHA present)
  - GitHub PR link (if PR number or URL is resolvable)
  - Console deploy/rollout details deep link (parameterized to service/region/time window)
- If deploy metadata lookup fails or times out, bot degrades gracefully:
  - render card with “Deploy context unavailable” + error category (timeout vs permission vs upstream error)
  - include fallback links (Console deploy timeline page) and a retry action
- Unit tests cover:
  - schema parsing for deploy metadata
  - link generation
  - truncation rules (Slack field length)
- E2E test (or mocked integration test) verifies the card renders in a thread and refresh action is idempotent.
implementation_notes:
Proposed implementation approach:
1) Data fetching
- Add DeployMetadataClient to incident-bot (or reuse existing internal client module) to fetch:
  - recent deploy events for (service, env, region)
- Prefer a single backend endpoint call that returns:
  - service, region, env
  - events[] with: started_at, finished_at, rollout_phase, canary_result, image_sha/image_tag, commit_sha, pr_url/pr_number, rollout_id
- Set strict timeout budget for the fetch (target 1.0s; hard cap 1.5s). If exceeded, return a degraded card.

2) Rendering
- New Slack block/card type: RecentDeploysCard
- Display format:
  - Header: “Recent deploys — <service> (<region>)”
  - For each deploy event: “<rollout_phase> • <canary_status> • <version> • <timestamp>”
  - Links row: Commit | PR | Rollout
- Truncation:
  - show max 3 events by default
  - if more are available, show “View more” action (modal/pagination handled in ENG-5425)

3) Reliability
- Cache deploy metadata per (service, region) for a short TTL (e.g., 60s) to avoid dogpiling during incidents.
- Emit structured logs for card completeness (present/missing) to support MTTR/context completeness measurement.

4) Ownership boundaries
- This ticket should not block on perfect PR resolution. If PR cannot be determined, commit + internal rollout link is sufficient.

Open questions (track in comments):
- Canonical mapping from deploy -> PR: do we rely on metadata from release pipeline vs GitHub search?
- How to represent partial rollouts (e.g., staged in 10% / 50% / 100%) in a short Slack-friendly way.
- Default time window: last 2h vs last 24h vs last N deploys.
comments: 2025-02-11 (Miles Thornton): Creating as top priority card for v2 beta. Multiple responders called out missing deploy context in #incidents; this is the quickest MTTR win.

2025-02-13 (Connor O'Brien): Deploy metadata export will include rollout_phase and canary verdict. PR link is best-effort; commit SHA will be reliable. Please don’t build GitHub search into the bot unless we have to (rate limits + slow).

2025-02-18 (Devon Price): Implemented initial card rendering behind feature flag `incident_bot_v2_recent_deploys_card`. Uses new DeployMetadataClient with 1.2s timeout and 60s cache. Added basic link generator for commit + rollout_id.
2025-02-20 (Rafael Mendes): Request: include rollback indication explicitly. If rollout_phase == ROLLBACK, highlight it (uppercase + label) so it pops during triage.

2025-02-24 (Devon Price): Added rollback highlight + canary result badges (PASS/FAIL/IN_PROGRESS/UNKNOWN). Added degraded-mode messaging: `Deploy context unavailable (timeout)` and always includes Console deploy timeline link.

2025-02-27 (Dylan Brooks): Review feedback: keep the card compact. Avoid long canary reason strings in the main message—truncate to 80 chars and put full text behind “View details” action (ties to ENG-5425 modal work).

2025-03-03 (Devon Price): Addressed compactness: truncated reason, show max 3 deploys, moved extra details to action payload. Added unit tests for parsing + truncation + link formatting. Marking In Review; please review PR incident-bot#1842.
